O Pāripātrī, you are free from disease; O Kṛṣikāraṇā, by the bank, according to your ability, I have been made into mud. O Mālikā, having washed me, place me in a basket.
Then, monks, that gardener addressed the tortoise with a verse:
"Much has been gathered by me for the king, and a great multitude of the three classes has assembled.
There, O auspicious tortoise, you shall sport in a basket fashioned as a casket."
Then, monks, that tortoise addressed the florist with a verse:
"Many are your accumulated [flowers], O King; the three classes have gathered in great numbers.
Intoxicated, you prattle on, O garland-maker! Eat the fine tortoise in oil!"

The Blessed One said: "O monks, it might occur to you that at that time, on that occasion, the Bhadrakalpa was another. It should not be viewed in this way. Why is that? O monks, at that time, on that occasion, I was that tortoise. At that time, on that occasion, the florist was another. Indeed, it should not be viewed in this way. Why is that? O monks, at that time, on that occasion, that florist was Māra Pāpīyān. Even then, I was liberated from the hands of that florist through my superior intelligence; even now, I am liberated from the realm of this Māra through my superior intelligence."
The Kacchapa-jātaka is completed.

"Moreover, monks, it is not only now that I was freed from his domain; on another occasion as well, I escaped from falling into his hands. The monks said, 'Was there another occasion, Blessed One? The Blessed One said, 'There was another occasion, monks.'"

Once upon a time, monks, in the distant past, on the shore of the ocean there was a great forest tract adorned with various groves and trees of diverse colors, rich in flowers and fruits, and abounding in *udumbara* trees. There lived a monkey, the leader of a large troop of monkeys. He dwelt in that forest grove together with his troop, in a place that was peaceful, secluded, frequented by many hundreds of deer and birds, and uninhabited by humans. That lord of monkeys lived on the ocean shore, eating *udumbara* fruits from a large *udumbara* tree that had abundant branches and foliage. Then a great crocodile came to that region from the sea; he sat there on the seashore. He was seen by the lord of monkeys. Upon seeing the crocodile, compassion arose in him: "Where indeed can these water-dwellers find flowers or fruits in the middle of the ocean? What if I were now to give some *udumbara* fruits to him? So he then shook down very large, ripe *udumbara* fruits—perfect in color and perfect in flavor—from that *udumbara* tree right before him, and as the fruits fell one after another, the crocodile ate them. In this way, the crocodile came again and again to that spot near the monkey. The lord of monkeys, for every one who arrived, would shake down *udumbara* fruits from the tree. Then both the monkey and the crocodile became affectionate toward one another. Now the crocodile’s wife, not seeing her husband, grew anxious: "Something must have happened to my husband; perhaps another female crocodile has been taken by him. Therefore, he has gone away from me and is sitting with her. She then asked her husband: "Where have you gone from me to sit? He said to her: "On the seashore, in such-and-such a place, in a great forest tract, there I have a monkey friend."

I shall remain here engaged in conversation and discourse with him. Then it occurred to that female crocodile: "As long as that monkey lives, this husband of mine will go there and remain in conversation with the monkey. Therefore, I shall have that monkey killed; once he is killed, this husband of mine will no longer go to that place. Then that female crocodile remained feigning illness. The male crocodile asked her: "My lady, what is your business? What is your suffering? What is your desire? Tell me, what shall I give you? Command me! She said to him: "Noble sir, I have a pregnancy-longing for a monkey’s heart. If I obtain a monkey’s heart, I shall live; if I do not obtain it, I have no life. He said to her: "Have faith! Where in this ocean is there a monkey to be found? If your desire is for some other aquatic creature, I shall provide one for you. She then said: "I have no desire for anything else; my desire is for a monkey’s heart. Provide that for me if you wish me to live. He tried to persuade her again and again: "Have faith, my lady! Where in the midst of these waters is there a monkey? She then said: "That monkey who is your friend on the seashore—bring the heart of that friend. He said: "Have faith! That monkey is my friend and my companion; how could I possibly tear out his heart? She then said: "If you cannot provide a monkey’s heart for me, I have no life. Now, that male crocodile, being thoroughly captivated by that female crocodile, said: "I am an aquatic creature, while that monkey is a land-dweller and a forest-dweller; where he roams, there I have no access. How then can I bring the heart of that monkey? As it has been said by the wise: [The rest of the verse follows].
A hundred is the measure of kṣatriyas, two hundred is the measure of brahmins,
a thousand is the measure of kings, but for women, the measure is infinite.

“O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with the teaching of the Dharma; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with the faultless teaching of the Dharma; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with the teaching of the Dharma; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with the faultless teaching of the Dharma; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with knowledge; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with vision; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with knowledge and vision; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with imperturbability; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with protection; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with excellence of prior birth; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with excellence of simultaneous birth; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with excellence of auspicious birth; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with excellence of supreme birth; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with excellence of eldest birth; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with excellence of best birth; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment?’”

"O Gautama, I would depart from you in disillusionment! O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in their prior aspirations; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in excellence; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in accumulation; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are skilled in support; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in equipment; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in the noble five-limbed concentration; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in the noble great five-limbed concentration; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in the noble five-fold knowledge; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in the noble great five-fold knowledge; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in one-pointedness of mind; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in the absence of strife (araṇā); what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Evil One, did it not occur to you: 'Beings of such a kind are perfected in crushing the army of enemies; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment?'"

“O Māra, wicked one, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with self-becoming; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Māra, wicked one, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with the nature of self-becoming; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Māra, wicked one, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with the supreme, foremost nature of Dharma; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Māra, wicked one, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with the accomplishment of merit; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Māra, wicked one, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these are endowed with the supreme, foremost perfection of beauty; what if I were to depart from the ascetic Gautama in disillusionment? O Māra, wicked one, did it not occur to you: ‘Beings such as these, being endowed with the perfection of beauty, are moreover difficult to overcome’? Behold, O Māra, wicked one, how great this transgression is! Standing to one side, the deities belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host roared out these eighty points directly to Māra, the wicked one. This is what the Blessed One said while staying at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain. And while this exposition was being spoken, the minds of five hundred monks were liberated from the outflows through non-clinging. With uplifted hearts, those monks rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Sūtra named Avalokita is completed.

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vaiśālī in the Āmrapālī grove, together with a great saṃgha of bhikṣus and a great host of bodhisattvas. Then the bhikṣu Viśuddhamati rose from his seat, draped his robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and [approached] where...

The Blessed One, having extended his joined palms toward him, said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One explain that which was surveyed by the Blessed One while he was a Bodhisattva, having approached the seat of awakening and stood upon the seat of awakening, for the benefit of the whole world and for the happiness of the whole world. That will be for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of a great multitude of beings—both gods and humans—and it will provide a great illumination of the Dharma for Bodhisattvas and Mahāsattvas; thus great consolation will be granted. Then, at that time, the monk Viśuddhamati spoke this verse:
How did you, O Light of the World, immeasurable and free from substrate,
cross over to the Nairañjanā for the benefit of all living beings?
O Great Hero, Tathāgata, Great Sage, please explain the signs that appeared there when the Supreme among Men was hurrying.
Just as the seat of enlightenment has been adorned by you, O Light of the World,
so please speak to me as I ask, for you are one who brings about welfare, benefit, and purpose.
Just as supreme enlightenment was attained by you, O shrine of the world, so too,
O Evil One, have you destroyed the Kinsman of Darkness along with his army.
O Self-Existent One, Essence of Beings, you possess ten supreme powers;

O Great Seer, honored a hundred times by men and gods, you illuminate all directions with the majesty of your supernormal power, O Caravan Leader. Just as the king of swans, white as the finest snow, pure, a Dhārtarāṣṭra, the best of excellent birds, with tireless body, flies through the cardinal and intermediate directions, even so do you travel, having made the hosts of gods, asuras, nāgas, and yakṣas dwell in the abodes of the Maruts.

[He is] the pillar of all crooked colors. Just as a burnt pillar is surpassed by a golden image, so does the Teacher surpass the entire world. His jewel-body is in full bloom with the marks [of perfection], just as the sky is filled with stars. There is no limit to the hundreds of thousands of merits of the Sugata; even a single name of his is beyond measure. There is no one equal to him in the whole world, so how could there be anyone superior? Thus he illuminates all ten directions on every side, like the thousand-rayed sun in the atmosphere. Your person, O One of Ten Powers, is adorned with the thirty-two marks of excellence; free from density, you shine like the moon in the month of Kārttika. Just as the eighty-four thousand [beings] are [adorned] by stars, so too are the other eighty-four [thousands] among the followers of the Teacher, by whom the voice of the Blessed One is taken up in its thousandfold components. By whomsoever the words of the Blessed One are grasped, from the mouth of the Blessed One the fragrance of sandalwood wafts forth.

Having filled the incomparable, immeasurable, and limitless Buddha-field, you have pacified the stubbornness, hatred, and delusion [of beings]. Even if the entire three-thousandfold world system were filled with mustard seeds, O Śikhīśiri, it might be possible for a wise person to count those mustard seeds in a single moment; yet it is not possible to count all the realms of sentient beings in the ten directions—those who, having smelled the fragrance of the Blessed One Candana, have attained the stage of patience (*kṣāntibhūmi*). O steadfast one, you are beyond compare; O hero of great compassion, you possess the power of great majesty and are a physician for sentient beings. O Protector, you have attained the state of one worthy of offerings (*dakṣiṇīya*); O Supreme Victor, Self-Arisen One, for those who go to you for refuge! Who indeed could ever find satiety in praising you? For such is the immeasurable power of the Blessed One. We go for refuge to you, the Subduer, the Unsubdued, whose infinite praises are sung, who has destroyed passion, and whose mind is peaceful. It might be possible to reach the end of space as it moves, or even to exhaust the ocean; but it is not possible to reach the end of your qualities.

O Conqueror, may you exhaust the measure of power; for thus is the Perfectly Awakened One, possessed of perfected strength. I ask the Lion among men, the Lord of Men, the one endowed with the ten powers, the immeasurable one: O Hero, whose passion is destroyed, whose mind is tranquil, purified by knowledge—[explain] to me this question concerning the non-attachment to the ten directions. O Benefactor, please answer my inquiry.
For immeasurable and inconceivable thousands of millions of eons,
the Omniscient One, the Supreme among Men, has practiced for the sake of others' welfare.
Generosity, ethical conduct, patience, and meditative absorptions were practiced,
and wisdom was cultivated in the past for many hundreds of millions of eons.
Whatever radiance belongs to fiery jewels, or that of lightning in the sky,
or even the radiance of the stars— all these become dull in color.
There is no god, nor nāga, nor yakṣa, nor kumbhāṇḍa, nor rākṣasa,
who possesses such a body as yours, O Leader of Men.

Worthy of worship by the best of gods and asuras, honored with prostrations by teachers, well-gathered, O Great Seer, light-maker, Lord of bipeds, essence of beings, supreme bull among men—a monument for humanity! Upon the forehead between the eyebrows, the circle of hair (*ūrṇā*) shines like a perfectly pure ray in the sky; it glows like the stainless moon on the full-moon night in the month of Kārtika. The Leader’s eyes are blue and stainless, resembling the color of a beautiful, choice lotus; his pure and auspicious radiance shines forth, bringing happiness to men and women. The teeth of the Lord of Men are stainless and white, well-formed, even, and like the finest snow of the Himalayas.

O Daśabala, your face is radiant with teeth that shine like petals; likewise, the Teacher’s tongue is pure and white, covered with youthful and delicate rays, possessing a supreme flavor, and it shines with a color equal to a young sprout. Divine, it brings conviction to many people. Your forehead, together with the eyebrows and face, is adorned with a web of light that bestows happiness, shining just like the moon. O Daśabala, the Blessed One’s hair upon the head is dark blue, well-composed, and pleasant. O Lion of the Śākyas, your neck shines like a golden conch-shell, and your arms, O Jina, are perfectly symmetrical. The Blessed One’s physical form is indestructible, preceded by the strength of a lion; it illuminates the world in all directions. O you of distinguished speech, ocean of the incomparable ripening of karma, speak these words! Having asked, the entire world bows down to you, won over and inspired by their ten-fingered palms joined in reverence.

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the monk Viśuddhamati: "Excellent, excellent, monk! It is indeed well of you, monk, that you consider it necessary to ask the Tathāgata about this matter. Your eloquence, monk, is splendid; your inquiry is noble, since you manifest such eloquence, monk. Indeed, the maturation of karma will manifest for those sons of good family who shall come to possess this Dharma-discourse. They shall not fall under the power of Māra, the Evil One, nor shall humans or non-humans find an opportunity to harm them. Why is that? Because, monk, those beings for whose sake you ask about this matter—the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas—are practitioners of sublime roots of merit. You, monk, considering it for the sake of beings, deem it necessary to ask the Tathāgata about this matter concerning the Bodhisattvas, the leaders of the world, who have set out upon the distinguished conduct toward all beings. You, monk, [are acting] for the sake of beings...

"You ask the Tathāgata about this matter concerning the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, the leaders of the world, who have set out endowed with skill in severing and analyzing all doubts. O Bhikṣu, for the sake of sentient beings, you ask the Tathāgata about this matter concerning the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, the leaders of the world, who are devoted to the excellence of giving, devoted to the excellence of patience, devoted to the excellence of meditation, and devoted to the excellence of wisdom. Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke this verse:
Having descended from the divine Tuṣita abode, he became a six-tusked elephant white as snow;
he entered the womb of the king’s chief queen, and then the three-thousandfold world system trembled.
Then, a vast radiance, golden in color, blazed forth throughout this entire thousandfold world-system,
reaching upward as far as the peak of existence, when the Conqueror entered the womb with full awareness.
Hundreds of thousands of Śakras and tens of millions of Brahmās constantly pay homage to the Victor dwelling within the noble womb;
they approach him by day and even at midnight, yet these beings never depart unless they have been dismissed.
And musical instruments resounded with a hundred thousand notes, filling the sky above with all the gods;
others, having cast aside divine sandalwood powder, held banners and parasols in their hands.
Divine and excellent flowers, including blue lotuses, rained down from the heavens.
Bees, cuckoos, and golden garlands [were present] until the Jina entered the womb with full awareness.
When you came as the Buddha, the essence of beings, Indra among the gods, you joyfully held out a distinguished,
most beautiful garment of Kāuśeya silk, resembling the color of Jāmbūnada gold;
and when the Bodhisattva, standing upon the earth, took seven steps with a joyful heart.
I shall indeed bring about in this world an incomparable end to old age and the process of death.
Then the earth shook in six ways, and a light was released in all directions;
divine sounds resounded in the sky, and there were eighty thousand deities.
And divine powders of sandalwood, beautiful with gold, rained down from the sky by the sons of the gods;
filled with joy and their hearts thrilled, the Maruts scattered mandārava flowers over the Bodhisattva.
Having reached the age of twenty-nine and having brought the world to maturity, the Bodhisattva renounced his kingdom and the seven precious jewels; clad in saffron robes, he became a Bodhisattva.
Having thus gone forth, the wise Bodhisattva practiced austerities for six years.
He entered the realm of Māgadha, and the daughter of a village headman beheld the Bodhisattva;
with a joyful heart, she took a golden bowl and a water-pitcher variegated with jewels.
Then the seer Bodhisattva performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), endowed with eight qualities and perfectly pure.
One should bring food endowed with strength, well-prepared by the gods, and fragrant;
and thus one should generate such a fervent desire, born of speed, thinking: "May I become a Buddha, armored with the primary marks."
Having abandoned this inferior state of desire, one should practice the pure and unblemished holy life;
one should avoid sensual pleasure, which causes suffering and is the root of disease, and should serve the Buddhas, who have destroyed passion and are free from defilements.
Having spoken such a verse as this, the daughter of the general, with a joyful heart, paid homage to the Bodhisattva with palms joined; shedding tears, she spoke these words:

King Bimbisāra has obtained a great gain; having attained freedom from sorrow, his sovereign power is increased, since this Bodhisattva dwells within his realm and today shall attain incomparable, supreme enlightenment.
Having eaten my meal, Krakucchanda, the Self-Existent One, shall go to the king of trees;
illuminating the ten directions on all sides like a sacrificial pillar of Jāmbūnada gold.
Whose name is Konāka, the one most worthy of great offerings—he, having eaten his meal, shall proceed to the seat of awakening;
with undaunted mind, immovable and unshakable, his body adorned with the primary marks.
At that time, even Kāśyapa— who possesses a body resembling Jāmbūnada gold—
having eaten my meal, that wise essence of beings shall go of his own accord to the best of trees, the lord of plants.

Those wise ones who, in this Fortunate Aeon, shall become incomparable objects of veneration—steadfast, with dust and defilements destroyed—I shall worship them all for the sake of incomparable awakening; indeed, I have no other desire whatsoever.
Those sons of the gods here in the atmosphere, let them sprinkle the Bodhisattva with sandalwood.
"Having attained her goal, the daughter of the general speaks these words, born from the impulse of joy."
You remembered your former abodes, Sujātā, conceiving pure love for the Bodhisattva;
thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, having eaten my meal, went to the foot of the Bodhi tree.

Then the Bodhisattva approached the Nairañjanā river and stood for a moment; with the soles of his feet level, he caused the earth to tremble. At that time, there was a great earthquake, terrifying and hair-raising, by which this trichiliocosm became as level as the palm of a hand. Sumeru, the king of mountains, the Cakravāḍa and Mahācakravāḍa mountains, Mount Nimindhara, Yugandhara, Īṣādhara, Khadiraka, Aśvakarṇa, Vinataka, Sudarśana—the seven mountain ranges—and likewise the intermediate islands and other black mountains, all sank down into the earth.

By the power of the Bodhisattva, the great oceans were stirred and became visible through the power of the Bodhisattva. At that time, this triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system was covered with lotuses made of Jāmbūnada gold, each the size of a wagon wheel, numbering hundreds of thousands, with hundreds of thousands of petals, and composed of blue beryl, musāragalva, and śirigarbha-piñjala; it was laid out like a checkerboard, and a great radiance appeared. By that radiance, the terrifying great hells were pacified, and all beings in those hells became happy. All beings born as animals became happy. All beings in the realm of Yama became happy, possessing minds of mutual loving-kindness through the power of the Bodhisattva. And by that great radiance, the entire triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system was illuminated. Furthermore, at that time, whatever palaces of the lords of gods, lords of nāgas, lords of yakṣas, and lords of garuḍas there were in the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system, they all became one unified radiance. Everywhere, they perceived the presence of the Bodhisattva’s own body. Furthermore, at that time, whatever gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, and kiṃnaras there were in the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system...

O great serpents, they all found no pleasure in their respective seats due to the majesty of the Bodhisattva. Unable to endure the splendor of the Bodhisattva, they all approached the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*), carrying flowers, garlands, perfumes, parasols, banners, musical instruments, incense, and ointments. Furthermore, at that time, Bodhisattvas of surpassing beauty from countless and immeasurable Buddha-fields, having manifested themselves in the guise of deities, stationed themselves in the sky above, holding divine blue lotuses (*utpala*), red lotuses (*padma*), and white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*). Furthermore, at that time, this triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system [was filled with] Śakra—

The earth was covered from its surface up to the peak of existence by hundreds of thousands of Jāmbūnada-gold lotuses the size of chariot wheels, with stalks of blue beryl and myriads of filaments like the heart-enclosures of *śirīṣa* flowers; and it was likewise filled from the ground up to the peak of existence with visiting Bodhisattvas, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.

Then indeed, in front of a great host of gods, the Bodhisattva crossed the river Nairañjanā. At that time, eighty koṭis of parasols made of Jāmbūnada gold appeared and remained above the Bodhisattva; eighty koṭis of parasols made of silver; eighty koṭis of parasols made of emerald (aśmagarbha); eighty koṭis of parasols made of elephant-essence (hastigarbha); eighty koṭis of parasols made of ruby (lohitaka); and eighty koṭis of parasols made of jewels appeared and remained above the Bodhisattva. Furthermore, there were eighty koṭis of nāgas, each nāga accompanied by a retinue of eighty koṭis of nāgas, holding red pearl flowers, who approached the Bodhisattva and honored him with the most supreme accumulation of merit.

Then indeed, the nāga king Kāla, accompanied by his own retinue, emerged from his own abode and approached the Bodhisattva; having bowed his head at the feet of the Bodhisattva and gazing at him with palms joined in reverence, he addressed him in verses:
Seeking awakening, the Bodhisattva, full of confidence,
having traversed the Nairañjanā River, approached the foot of the tree of awakening.
Resounding with the cries of various flocks of birds and adorned with excellent trees.
Endowed with excellent flowers and fruits, as far as the triple-thousandfold world system extends.
Where those illuminators of the world arrived and attained enlightenment:
Krakucchanda, Konākamuni, and the great sage Kāśyapa.
The Light of the World, the Leader of the World,
that supreme Sage of the Śākyas, the kinsmen of the Sun, approached that place.
All those hosts of gods, joyful and delighted in mind,
made that earth like a mass of clouds of flowers.
Having come to their own abodes, the Śuddhāvāsa deities assembled and paid homage to the Leader of the World; they circumambulated the Bodhisattva.
Adorn the seat of awakening with divine and human mandārava flowers— exquisite and most excellent.
Then all the trees in the forest at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) bowed down toward that preeminent region,
which had been frequented by previous Buddhas.
And the deity who was dwelling in the tree at the seat of awakening,
upon seeing the Bodhisattva, let out a superhuman cry.
You waved a divine cloth and sprinkled excellent sandalwood;
you showered that bull among men with divine powders of precious gems.
Winds bearing various kinds of divine and human fragrances blew toward the seat of enlightenment from all four directions.
And divine, beautiful musical instruments were played in the sky,
performing various kinds of music that were sweet-sounding and enchanting.
A most great radiance arose from the rays of the seat of awakening,
by which the entire world of the gods was immediately suffused.
The divine celestial palaces made of jewels became dull in color by the rays of the Bodhisattva’s Jāmbūnada gold.
Thousands of sons of gods, possessing great supernatural power, stood in the sky and showered the Bodhisattva with mandārava flowers.
Having heard the incomparable voice of the Great Seer, the Naga Kāla,
accompanied by the Naga maidens, was thrilled, delighted, and satisfied.
Having abandoned all divine pleasures of play and delight, he has come here;
looking toward the four directions, he beholds the bull among men.
Having honored Vairocana in the sky, who is surrounded by all rays of light,
the Bodhisattva, joyful and contented, addressed him.
O Supreme among Men, such were the marks of the previous Buddhas— of Krakucchanda, of Konākamuni, the best of men, and likewise of the Jina Kāśyapa, the Tathāgata, the Supreme among Men.
The feet of those great seers are even, webbed, and well-set;
they have the color of lac-juice applied to them, possess wheels,
and the soles of their feet are adorned with svastikas.
Upon all the toes of their feet, the *nandyāvarta* patterns are raised;
they shine as the Lords of the World traverse the variegated earth.
O Lord, your feet are unrestrained, just as you yourself are;
they do not shine with prominent ankles, and your toes are well-knit.
The feet of the Lords of the World, as they traverse the variegated earth, have long toes, copper-colored nails, webbed fingers and toes, and prominent ankles.
Your shanks shall be like those of the enī deer, resembling the interior of a lotus;
with concealed knees and ankles, you shall likewise become a benefactor to the world.
The arms of those great seers were like the trunks of elephants;
their upper bodies were like those of lions, and they were as well-proportioned as the banyan tree.
Like refined gold, beautiful with a golden complexion,
she touched her knees with her hands while her body remained unbent.
For just as the hips of those kings of deer are rounded and well-proportioned,
so too is the sheathed private organ of the king of horses.
Their conduct was pure white, their knees were well-proportioned, and they had deep navels; such were those former Buddhas, the great seers.
The bodies of those great seers were untouched even by a speck of dust.
And your skin is smooth, O Lord, just like that of you, sir.
Each of your hairs grew singly, and you possessed a row of body hair with tips pointing upward; likewise, O Benefactor of the World, your body hair was blue and curled to the right.
Their shoulders were well-rounded, and their eyebrows were like those of a bull; these lords had broad, straight limbs and were possessed of these [eight] secondary marks.
With arms like the coils of a serpent, tapering and free from arrogance,
you possess such a Nārāyaṇa-like firmness as is yours.
With prominent nails and copper-colored nails, resembling the peaks of Mount Kailāsa,
their bodies were exceedingly beautiful, adorned with these elevated marks.
Their necks are like conch shells, rising in smooth gradation; those Lords have jaws like a lion's and are supreme among those who possess the sense of taste.
Those great seers had forty well-rounded teeth;
their canine fangs were as white as yours, O Blessed One.
With their broad and slender tongues, they covered their entire faces;
they also wiped both the tips of their ears and their noses.
The speech of those great seers, who possess all-seeing vision, is perfectly complete in its eight aspects, truthful, and should be understood by all living beings.
Your voice was like that of Brahmā, with a tone like the song of the kalaviṅka bird;
it had the resonance of a drum and was truly lovely to hear.
Just as a golden lotus shines,
so did the faces of the Protectors, the kinsmen of the Sun, radiate light.
The eyes of those great seers were long and deep blue,
and their prominent noses shone like golden sacrificial posts.
Between the eyebrows of those great sages of noble birth,
there appeared a radiant *ūrṇā*, soft like cotton.
And her face was like a great flame, or like the full moon on the night of the full moon;
and all the directions were illuminated by that radiance from her jewel-adorned neck.
Your hair is dark blue and soft, resembling kācilindika cloth;
all the hairs curl to the right, for you, O Blessed One, are a benefactor to the world.
Those Protectors have cranial protuberances on their heads just like yours;
their heads are not to be looked upon even by gods or asuras.
For those Buddhas possess great radiance;
they outshine [all] with their rays, just as the moon is outshone by its own light when eclipsed by the King of Comets.
Having seen these and other signs and characteristics of the Bodhisattva, they all spoke these words.
Since those sons of the gods have come forth to honor you,
O Great Hero, there is no doubt that today you will become a Buddha.
With a concentrated mind, having taken up the weapon of wisdom, you shall cut through the unvanquished, web-like craving that leads to existence— the bond of Māra.
Today, O Supreme among Men, having attained enlightenment, you will utterly shake off the fire of passion that completely envelops you with all remaining afflictions.
The outer robe, the bowl, and likewise the color of the monastic garment—
just as they were seen by the Protectors, so too are they yours, O benefactor of the world.
All such persons as these turn to the right;
just as you walk like a lion today, so shall you become a Buddha.
Like a mountain, unshakable, and like a Conqueror,
having established himself at the seat of awakening, he exerted firm vigor.
Having heard those words spoken by Kālanāga,
he was pleased and, with an uplifted and joyful mind, approached the foot of the Bodhi tree.
Having heard that incomparable sound, the mighty Naga Kāla rose up from his abode with great speed toward the Bodhisattva.
Having joined his palms with all ten fingers extended,
he praised the Hero of Wisdom as he was proceeding toward the seat of enlightenment.
Just as these gentle winds will always blow pleasantly—
fragrant and delightful, neither too hot nor too cold.
And just as these deities rained down this shower of flowers:
"O Sugata, O Supreme among Men, you shall attain the state of an Arhat."
O worthy one, turning to the right, satisfied and delighted,
with a joyful and exultant mind, go forth while emitting bliss.
Just as thousands of musical instruments resound, filling the sky above with the voices of deities,
you will be born with a surge of joyful and delighted mind, becoming a Buddha distinguished throughout the entire world.
Just as no other light above the celestial palaces shines forth, and all [other] colors become dimmed;
and just as the earth trembles in six ways—today you shall become an incomparable one worthy of offerings.
And as they joyfully waved their garments, having shattered the host of Māra and Bhīṣma, they held up parasols, banners, and flags, saying: "You shall become a Buddha; I have no doubt."
And as the sweet-sounding drums resound, filling the entire expanse of the sky with their echoes,
and as the hosts of gods rain down flowers, you shall become a self-arisen one in this world together with its gods.
And just as thousands of gods, with joyful hearts, joined their palms in the sky and praised him, saying:
"O one of golden radiance, most distinguished, you shall become a Buddha, a worthy recipient of offerings, the supreme teacher of men."

Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva approached the foot of the tree. At that time, the entire seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) was draped with bundles of silk ribbons and cords; it was adorned with raised banners and pennants, decorated with hundreds of thousands of parasols, variegated with strings of jewels, perfumed with incense, surrounded by jewel-trees, strewn with layers of robes, scattered with sandalwood powder, and made beautiful by heaps of gems. Furthermore, at that time, many hundreds of thousands of gods, stationed in the sky above, paid homage to the Bodhisattva while holding incense. Holding parasols, banners, and pennants, they paid homage to the Bodhisattva. Holding divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water lilies, and white lotuses, they paid homage to the Bodhisattva. Holding divine sandalwood powder, they paid homage to the Bodhisattva. Holding divine jewel powder and divine jewel flowers, they gazed with unblinking eyes and paid homage to the Bodhisattva. Other deities perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of gold, according to their own individual inclinations. Other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of silver; other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of lapis lazuli; other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of crystal; other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of emerald; other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of the seven precious substances; other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of hundreds of thousands of jewels—just so, according to their respective inclinations. Other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of red sandalwood; other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being made of aloe-wood sandalwood; other gods...

Some perceive the Bodhi tree as consisting of the jewels desired by one another. Other gods perceive the Bodhi tree as made of yellow sandalwood; other gods perceive the Bodhi tree as made of lion-sandalwood; other gods perceive the Bodhi tree as made of essence-sandalwood. Just so, according to their respective inclinations, some gods perceive the Bodhi tree as made of mountain-essence sandalwood; other gods perceive the Bodhi tree as made of divine agallochum-sandalwood; other gods perceive the Bodhi tree as made of precious gems. Some gods perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with all kinds of jewels; others perceive it as variegated with precious gems; others perceive it as adorned with divine blue beryl; others perceive it as variegated with *musāragalva* gems; others perceive it as variegated with *aśmagarbha* (emerald) gems; others perceive it as variegated with *hastigarbha* gems; others perceive the Bodhi tree as variegated with various precious gems; others perceive the Bodhi tree as variegated with *suprabhāsa* (splendidly radiant) gems; others perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with nectar-like *aśmagarbha* gems; others perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with *samantacandra* (all-pervading moon) gems; others perceive it as adorned with *sucandra* (beautiful moon) gems; others perceive it as adorned with the radiance of the sun; others perceive it as variegated with crystal; others perceive it as adorned with *sūryavikrānta* (sun-transcending) gems; others perceive it as adorned with the radiance of the moon; others perceive it as adorned with the radiance of the stars; others perceive it as adorned with the radiance of lightning; others perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with *samantāloka* (all-illuminating) gems; others perceive it as adorned with *muktāprabha* (pearl-radiant) gems; others perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with *muktāprabha* gems; others perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with *apratihataprabha* (unimpeded radiance) gems; others perceive it as adorned with *ratnasamucchraya* (jewel-protuberances); others perceive it as adorned with gems that are the foremost in all worlds; others perceive it as adorned with *śakrābhilagna* (Indra’s-clinging) gems; others perceive it as [adorned] with jewel-leaves...

Some gods perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with *uragagarbha* jewel-gems; others perceive it as adorned with *candana-prabha* gems; others perceive it as adorned with *lohitākṣa* gems; others perceive it as adorned with *gajapati* jewel-gems; others perceive it as adorned with jewel-gems given by Maheśvara; others perceive it as adorned with *rasaka* gems; others perceive it as adorned with jewel-gems given by Maheśvara; others perceive it as adorned with *rasaka* gems; others perceive it as adorned with *gomedaka* jewel-gems; and other gods perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with *śaśa* jewel-gems. Others perceive it as adorned with *lālāṭika* jewel-gems; others perceive it as adorned with *śirigarbha* jewel-gems; and others perceive the Bodhi tree as adorned with *tālīka* jewels and various other divine jewel-gems.

Those gods whose roots of merit were to ripen for unsurpassed perfect enlightenment perceived the Bodhi tree according to their respective roots of merit. They perceived the Bodhi tree adorned with blue pearl necklaces, red pearl necklaces, white pearl necklaces, neck-ornaments, golden threads, earrings, signet rings, bracelets, bangles, anklets, head-wraps, finger-seals, armlets, jeweled bands, silk bands, flower garlands, golden armlets, jewel necklaces, gold chains, mandārava garlands, swan-garlands, lion-vines, diamond-shaped ornaments, svastikas, and with these and other celestial ornaments. Those gods whose roots of merit were awakened upon seeing the Bodhi tree perceived the Bodhi tree as well-adorned; others perceived the Bodhi tree as adorned with these and other ornaments as previously described. Among them, some gods perceived the Bodhi tree as one *yojana* in height; other gods [perceived it] as five *yojanas* in height; others [perceived it] as ten *yojanas* in height.

Some gods perceived the Bodhi tree as being twenty *yojanas* in height; others as thirty *yojanas* in height; others as forty *yojanas* in height; and other gods perceived the Bodhi tree as fifty *yojanas* in height. Still others perceived the Bodhi tree as one hundred *yojanas* in height; they perceived the Bodhi tree in height according to their own respective knowledge. There are gods who perceive the Bodhi tree as one thousand *yojanas* in height. There are long-lived gods who, having performed meritorious services for previous Victors, perceive the Bodhi tree as one hundred thousand *yojanas* in height. There are sons of gods who, having brought forth roots of merit, perceive the Bodhi tree as high as the very peak of existence (*bhavāgra*). Therein, some gods saw a lion throne at the foot of the Bodhi tree, fashioned from every kind of jewel, divine and many *yojanas* in height, spread with celestial cloth, covered with a net of jewels, and adorned with a network of tinkling bells. Other gods saw a lion throne one hundred thousand *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne one thousand *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne two hundred and fifty *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne one hundred *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne fifty *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne thirty *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne twenty *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne ten *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne four *yojanas* in height. Other gods saw a lion throne three *yojanas* in height. Other gods [saw a lion throne] two *yojanas* in height...

Some gods saw the lion throne as one *nāli* in height; other gods saw the lion throne as one *yojana* in height; other gods saw the lion throne as three *krośas* in height; other gods saw the lion throne as two *krośas* in height; other gods saw the lion throne as one *krośa* in height; other gods saw the lion throne at the foot of the Bodhi tree as seven *tālas* in height; other gods [saw it] as six *tālas*, others as five *tālas*, others as four *tālas*, others as three *tālas*, others as two *tālas*, and others as just one *tāla* in height. Other gods saw the lion throne as seven *pauruṣeyas* in height; other gods saw the lion throne as six *pauruṣeyas* in height; others [saw it] as five *pauruṣeyas*, others as four *pauruṣeyas*, others as three *pauruṣeyas*, and others as two *pauruṣeyas*. Other gods saw the lion throne at the foot of the Bodhi tree as merely one *puruṣa* in height. Therein, those beings who were inclined toward the coarse saw the Bodhisattva seated upon a bed of grass, thinking: "Having sat upon this bed of grass, the Bodhisattva will awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Then, moreover, the Bodhisattva, having approached the foot of the Bodhi tree in the presence of the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, circumambulated the Bodhi tree three times to the right. Recalling the former Tathāgatas, he sat down, having assumed the cross-legged posture, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him. And while the Bodhisattva was thus seated at the foot of the Bodhi tree, the circle of his face shone, blazed, and radiated, just like the orb of the sun spread across the great trichiliocosm. By its brilliance, the entire great trichiliocosm became dimmed in color. Just as...

Just as a polished pillar of black lac before a golden image does not shine, does not gleam, and does not become radiant, even so the great trichiliocosm was eclipsed by the splendor of the Bodhisattva. There, the sons of the gods from the earth up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven saw the Bodhisattva seated there; the gods of the earth likewise saw the Bodhisattva as being right there with them. Similarly, in the atmosphere, the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin heavens, as well as those in the realm of Māra, perceived the Bodhisattva seated upon his lion-throne. Likewise, Brahmā, the gods of the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Mahābrahmā, Ābhā, Ābhāsvara, Śubha, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Bṛhatphala, Avṛha, Atapa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha heavens perceived the Bodhisattva seated upon his lion-throne. Furthermore, all those beings dwelling within the limits of the great trichiliocosm who were endowed with roots of merit perceived the Bodhisattva seated upon his lion-throne. And those beings belonging to the desire realm who had planted roots of merit and performed services for previous Victors did not see Māra, nor did they perceive him, as they offered worship to the Bodhisattva and paid homage to him through the power of the Bodhisattva.

Then indeed Māra, the Evil One, perceived his own power to be dimmed and saw that the entire great trichiliocosm was split asunder toward where the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva was. He trained himself thus: "I shall not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening so long as I have not defeated Māra, the Evil One, who has arrived with his army fully arrayed. Let it not be thought by beings that this is no marvel—that Māra was subdued by one who has attained awakening; and let the Bodhisattva demonstrate his own strength through a miracle of supernatural power to all beings."

Desiring to demonstrate this before the world of Vaka, [the Bodhisattva] has thus attained such firm power, momentum, and supernatural might (*ṛddhi*). Thinking, "Having trained in my footsteps, they will likewise resolve their minds toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment," Māra the Evil One—suffering, dejected, and pierced by the arrow of grief—conceived the idea that the Bodhisattva was his rival king. He mobilized the fourfold army of Māra and, having traveled many hundreds of *yojanas*, approached the foot of the Bodhi tree, thinking, "I shall see the Bodhisattva. Yet he was unable to see the Bodhisattva, for his vision had become clouded. If the Bodhisattva were to open his mouth wide, by the power with which the Bodhisattva was endowed, even if this great trichiliocosm world-system were made of diamond and mountain peaks, the Bodhisattva could reduce that world-system to atoms and toss it across incalculable world-systems, yet not a single atom would ever coincide with another. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva perceived within Māra’s assembly many beings who possessed roots of merit (*kuśalamūla*) and saw that upon witnessing such a miraculous display of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*), they would resolve their minds toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Perceiving this purpose, the Bodhisattva waited, thinking: "I shall not attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment until I have conquered Māra along with his forces and vehicles. Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
Just as the Self-Existent One, the King of the Śākyas, a being of perfect purity, stood at the foot of the Bodhi tree,
beautiful to behold like a golden image.
Like Jāmbūnada gold, he is free from all afflictions.
The quarters became filled with radiance, and Māra was terrified, fallen into distress,
thinking: "What indeed will happen to me?"
I find no delight in this celestial mansion.
All the celestial palaces were the color of the sky; they were the finest of mansions,
made of excellent sandalwood, with golden threads, crystal, and coral.
May I indeed not fall from this state today!
The windows are clearly visible with beautiful half-moons, and the inner chambers are inlaid with musāragalva; such is the preeminent palace of Vairocana in the world.
Was there light, will there be light, or is it indeed today?
The crown has fallen from my head,
and today my auspicious radiance has vanished; the celestial music of the apsarases has ceased for me.
May I indeed not fall from this place today!
Just as celestial palaces in the sky are rendered dull in color by Jāmbūnada gold,
so too are these divine palaces [dimmed].
When the Bodhisattva had ascended [the mountain] Jimhā.
And you have seen the Blessed One, the Self-Existent, seated like an invincible lion,
the pure essence, the essence of all beings in the world.
He shone like a sacrificial post made of Jāmbūnada gold.
The gods, established in heaven, wearing necklaces of liberation and beautiful golden shells, delightful to behold,
were overjoyed as they took up golden threads.
They adorned the Bodhi tree of the Blessed One.
And auspicious svastikas, half-moons,
and lion-vines adorned the Bodhi tree; and having seized lightning-like radiance and jewels, they stood there.
The joyful sons of the gods adorn it.
Having taken up the moon-light jewel, having taken up the sun-loved jewel,
and having taken up the Vairocana precious gem;
They adorn the Bodhi tree of the Blessed One.
And having taken up pearls and jewels that were radiant,
beautiful to behold, and illuminating,
they became filled with joy, their hearts glad and thrilled.
They adorn the Bodhi tree of the Blessed One.
Having taken up the *samantacandra* jewel-gems and the *ratnāvalī*,
which is most beautiful and lovely to behold, and having taken up the *gomedaka* jewel-gems;
They adorned the Bodhi tree of the Blessed One.
Others, having taken hold of Śubhalohitākṣā,
and having taken hold of the jewel Śirigarbhaśuddhā;
They adorn the Bodhi tree of the Blessed One.
And those with red limbs,
having taken up rucaka gems, were Maheśvaras of most beautiful complexion; and having taken up karketana jewels, they shone.
They adorned the Bodhi tree of the Blessed One.
